blocks.body: Lincoln Park homes have all three. Older greystones and frame houses often have masonry fireplaces, some converted to gas logs. Many renovations added direct-vent units that vent through a wall and use a sealed glass front. Others have inserts that fit inside an old firebox. Each has different parts and service needs. Tell us what you have, or show us a photo, and we'll come prepared.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of Fireplace Work
blocks.body: A service visit is simple. A failed part depends on the fireplace type and model. Running gas to a masonry fireplace depends on the route through the building. We diagnose and quote a flat price.

blocks.h2: Gas Fireplace Questions From Lincoln Park Homeowners

items.q: Can my old fireplace be converted to gas?
items.preview: Often, if the chimney is sound.
items.answer: Often. The chimney must be in good shape. We run the gas line and install the valve.

items.q: Why won't my pilot stay lit?
items.preview: A dirty pilot or weak thermocouple.
items.answer: Usually a dirty pilot or weak thermocouple or thermopile.

items.q: Does my gas log fireplace need the damper open?
items.answer: Yes. Vented gas logs need a fixed damper opening.

items.q: When should I service my fireplace?
items.answer: Early fall, before the first cold night.

items.q: Does a direct-vent fireplace need the damper open?
items.preview: No, it has its own vent.
items.answer: No. It vents through its own pipe, not the chimney.

items.q: How much does gas fireplace repair cost in Lincoln Park?
items.preview: It depends on the part. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what failed and the type of fireplace. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
